doc.title: Houston Person Part 2 interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, October 2, 1998 [interview 2 of 2]

title: What swing is and the loss of dancing
summary: Asked to define swing, Person says it is the element that makes the body move, and laments that jazz audiences now must sit still, with people leaving to go dance.

story.theme_name: Playing for dancers: dance bands and the dances themselves
story.community_name: Dancing to the band: quadrilles, waltzes and dance sets

blocks.x: Okay. It’s early in the interview, but I’m going to ask you a hard question. You said you like anything that swings. Can you define that?
Okay. That was a short answer.

No. Swing — well to me swing contributes to an element in jazz that has been left out now. That’s why we have problems, is the element of dance and it makes the body move, and makes your feet move and makes you respond. That’s what swing is, I guess the little thing your body is — you go, if you shake your head or whatever you do, but there’s a certain swing, an element that makes the body want to move. And now when you go to hear jazz you’ve got to sit still and you can’t dance, you can’t have fun.
Yeah or somebody across from you will tell you shhh, shhh.
Well if tomorrow night let’s say you’re in this jazz club in Utica, how would you feel if people started to get up and dance?

Yeah. To me that’s a part of it. That makes it complete. That’s why when you’re playing in a jazz club and people are leaving like at eleven o’clock, I’ll say like, “where are you going?” “Oh we’re going somewhere where we can dance.” Now years ago it wasn’t that way. You know, you’d dance.
